meta.site.description: An open network for communities that host themselves. Voice, text and end-to-end encrypted messaging across independent servers.
footer.tagline: Built for players. Owned by no one.
footer.optional: This directory is optional. Wavvon works without it.
home.hero.title: An open network for communities that host themselves
home.hero.body: Voice, text and end-to-end encrypted messaging across independent servers. Your identity is a keypair you hold — no accounts, no company in the middle, no central server to shut down.
home.hero.meta: open source · AGPL-3.0 · nothing to install
home.what.title: What is Wavvon?
home.what.body: A community runs a hub — one Rust binary and a database, on hardware they chose. Hubs talk to each other. You bring one key to all of them.
home.feature.voice.title: Voice and text together
home.feature.voice.body: Every channel is both. Opus over QUIC with noise suppression, push-to-talk, per-person volume, proximity voice, screen share and webcam.
home.feature.dms.title: Messages the server cannot read
home.feature.dms.body: Direct messages, one-to-one and group, are end-to-end encrypted. Hubs relay ciphertext — including when it crosses to another hub.
home.feature.federation.title: Hubs that federate
home.feature.federation.body: Independent communities form alliances and share channels, without either side handing over its members, its data, or its moderation.
home.feature.identity.title: One key, everywhere
home.feature.identity.body: An Ed25519 keypair with a 24-word recovery phrase. Pair your other devices with a QR code. Nothing to reset, nobody to ask.
home.start.title: Where do you start?
home.start.join.title: Find a community
home.start.join.body: Browse the hubs that chose to be listed, or paste an address someone gave you. Every hub serves its own client in the browser, so there is nothing to install first.
home.start.host.title: Run a hub
home.start.host.body: A hub runs on your own server: one container and a PostgreSQL database. You keep the data, the moderation and the decisions about who belongs.
home.start.host.aside: or let somebody host it for you →
home.start.build.title: Write a client or a bot
home.start.build.body: The whole protocol is plain HTTP and WebSocket, specified in an OpenAPI document. No SDK required, no partner programme, no key to apply for.
home.noserver.title: There is no Wavvon server
home.noserver.body1: Nothing in the network routes through us. A hub keeps working if this site disappears, if the project stops, or if we turn out to be idiots. That is not a promise about our intentions — it is a property of how it is built.
home.noserver.body2: This directory is a convenience. It cannot moderate a hub, suspend one, rank one higher for money, or see who joins what. Hubs publish themselves to it, signed with their own key, and can stop at any time.
home.guarantee.data.title: Your data lives on your hub
home.guarantee.data.body: Messages, uploads and members are in that community's own database, under their backup policy.
home.guarantee.protocol.title: The protocol is documented, not reverse-engineered
home.guarantee.protocol.body: HTTP and WebSocket, with an OpenAPI spec kept in step with the routes.
home.guarantee.licence.title: Every part is AGPL-3.0
home.guarantee.licence.body: Server, clients and this directory. Fork it, audit it, run a private copy of the whole thing.
home.guarantee.young.title: It is young, and says where it falls short
home.guarantee.young.body: There is a written comparison against the closed alternatives, including the parts we lose.
home.cta.title: Go find somewhere to hang out
home.cta.body: Or paste a hub address straight into your browser, if someone already gave you one.
hubs.title: Hubs
hubs.intro: Communities that chose to be listed. Each entry was published and signed by the hub itself, and can be pulled by it at any time. Plenty of hubs are not here at all — being listed is optional, and so is this page.
hubs.facet.language_note: Whatever the listed hubs speak. The list is not a menu we curate — it grows as hubs arrive.
hubs.empty.filtered: No hubs match those filters yet.
hubs.empty.none: Nobody has listed a hub here yet. Hubs publish themselves, so this fills up on its own.
hubs.cta.title: Nothing here fits?
hubs.cta.body: A hub is one container and a database. Run your own and it works whether or not it ever appears on this page.
hub.note: Everything on this page was written and signed by the hub itself. This directory does not inspect it, rank it, or vouch for it — it only checks that the signature matches the key.
hub.browser_note: Every hub serves its own web client. Nothing to install, no account here.
hub.wrong.title: Something wrong?
hub.wrong.body: This directory does not probe hubs, so a dead address stays listed until someone says so.
hub.no_power: This directory has no power over this hub. It cannot moderate it, suspend it, or see who joins.
hub.report.subject: Broken listing: {name}
clients.title: Clients
clients.intro: A client is anything that speaks the protocol, and the protocol is plain HTTP and WebSocket — so anyone can write one, in any language, with whatever taste they have. These are the ones people published. Your key and your hubs come with you whichever you pick.
clients.facet.language_note: This list is whatever the clients declare, so it grows on its own. Each one is translated by whoever maintains it — none covers every language, ours included.
clients.empty.none: No client has been listed yet. The official web client ships with every hub either way.
clients.cta.title: Written one?
clients.cta.body: Listings are signed with your own key, the way hubs publish themselves. Nobody approves it, and only your key can change or remove it.
client.supports_note: Declared by the maintainer in the listing, not tested by this directory. If something here is wrong, report it.
client.downloads_note: Downloads come from the maintainer's own release page. This directory does not host or scan binaries.
client.key_note: The key is the identity. It proves the same person published every version of this listing — not who they are.
client.language_note: Each client is translated by whoever maintains it, so coverage differs from one to the next.
client.disclaimer: This directory did not build, review or audit this client. Treat it like any other program you install.
bots.title: Bots
bots.intro.before: A bot is an Ed25519 key that speaks the same API you do. To add one, copy its public key and paste it into your hub under
bots.intro.after: . Nothing is installed on the hub, and the bot only sees the channels you give it.
bots.facet.tag_note: Bots pick their own tags when they publish, so this list is as messy or as tidy as their authors are.
bots.empty.none: No bot has been published yet. A bot is a keypair and a webhook — nothing to approve.
bots.cta.title: A bot is just a keypair and a webhook
bots.cta.body: No approval, no token to request from us. Generate a key, answer the webhook, publish the listing signed with that key.
bot.declared_note: Declared by the author in the listing. Your hub is what actually enforces it — a bot cannot take a permission you did not grant, whatever its listing says.
bot.runs_note: A bot runs on its author's machine, not on your hub. Yours sends it events over a webhook and it answers over the same API a person would use. Nothing is installed, and removing it is one click.
bot.add.title: Add it to your hub
bot.add.step3: Pick the channels it may see, and confirm.
bot.add.note: Needs the Bots permission on your hub. You are not signing up for anything here.
bot.disclaimer: This directory did not write, review or run this bot. Everything above is what its author declared.
capability.commands.meaning: Registers its commands in the channels you add it to.
capability.post-messages.meaning: Writes into the channels you add it to.
capability.read-messages.meaning: Sees the conversation, not only the commands aimed at it.
capability.moderate.meaning: Can time out, kick or ban, within the roles you give it.
capability.mini-apps.meaning: Opens an embedded view inside the client.
providers.title: Hosting providers
providers.intro: Running a hub means running a server, and not everybody wants to. These companies will run one for you. They are other people's businesses making their own offer — this directory does not vet them, take a cut, or stand behind anything they promise.
providers.how.title: How this list works
providers.how.body: Unlike hubs, clients and bots, nobody publishes into this page. It is a file in the directory's own repository, edited by hand — so running your own directory means curating your own list.
providers.empty.filtered: No provider on this list has a free tier.
providers.empty.none: Nobody is offering Wavvon hosting yet. Until somebody does, running a hub yourself is one container and a PostgreSQL database — the operator guide walks it end to end.
providers.note: A hosted hub is still your hub — the same software, the same keys, and the same right to move it somewhere else. What you are paying for is somebody else running the server. Read what a provider says about backups and about what happens when you leave, because nobody here checks either.
providers.cta.title: Rather run it yourself?
providers.cta.body_before: One container and a PostgreSQL database.
providers.cta.body_after: writes the compose file and the password for you, on your own machine.
docs.title: Docs
docs.intro: Every design decision, protocol detail and operational procedure, written down. The same documents the project works from — not a marketing rewrite of them.
docs.libraries.ts: TypeScript — the same, for clients and bots
docs.libraries.note: They will live on crates.io and npm. This page will link to them rather than mirror a registry that already exists.
